solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Netherlander's wife to west of island

indicators.note: in an across entry the western piece is written first, so this puts the wife before the island

parts.note: 'old Dutch' is Cockney slang for a wife, so Dutch alone can mean wife
the Isle of Man, the crossword's favourite island

explanation.surface: A man from the Netherlands, his wife living to the west of some island.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Netherlander stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. 'Old Dutch' (wife) is Cockney slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Netherlands is commonly called a Dutchman, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Extremely dodgy, unpleasant succession of rulers

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, taken here from dodgy

parts.note: something unpleasant is nasty

explanation.surface: A line of kings whose reign was extremely dodgy and unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty is a line of hereditary rulers from one family, one succeeding another.

clue.text: Play absorbing district attorney at the present time

indicators.note: absorbing means the first word takes the second into its middle

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it
DA is the standard abbreviation for a US district attorney

explanation.surface: A district attorney caught up in a play being staged right now.
explanation.definitionFit: Today, as an adverb, means nowadays, in the current period or this very day.

clue.text: Scatty, like a fast mover in form?

definitions.meaning: scatty means foolishly rash or scatterbrained

definitions.text: like a fast mover in form?
definitions.meaning: a hare is a fast mover and a form is a hare's nest; read in two parts, the answer suggests a hare's head

explanation.walkthrough: A hare's resting place in long grass is called its form, which helps the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Hare-brained describes rash, foolish behaviour, a common idiom for scatty people.

clue.text: One not identified turned up in academy — no name

indicators.note: turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words academy and no name

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An unnamed person turns up at an academy whose name is withheld.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'turned up' reads the hidden letters MYNONA from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: An anonym is a person whose name is kept hidden, an unnamed or unidentified individual.

clue.text: Type to be looked for, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals the word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: something being looked for is sought

explanation.surface: A type of person whom everyone is said to be seeking.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A sort is a kind or variety, a direct synonym of type.

clue.text: Sumptuous work loaned by university

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work
something loaned is lent

explanation.surface: A lavish piece of work on loan from a university collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent and sumptuous both describe lavish, luxurious richness.

clue.text: Be inclined to adopt right fashion

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the first word takes the letter for right inside it

parts.note: to tend is to be inclined to do something

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to follow whatever fashion is right at the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a current fashion or style that many follow.

clue.text: In outskirts of Namur, a detective's lowest point

indicators.note: In puts the following pieces inside the outskirts
the outskirts are the edges, the first and last letters of Namur

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector; the 's is just 'is', joining to the definition

explanation.surface: A detective in the suburbs of the Belgian city of Namur hits rock bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: Namur is a Belgian city; only its edge letters N and R are used.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the very bottom, the worst moment of any process.

clue.text: Little-known old boy's priest in Paris

parts.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil; with the 's it gives OBS
a curé is a French parish priest

explanation.surface: A former pupil's priest working in Paris whom nobody has heard of.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure means not well known, unfamiliar to most people.

clue.text: Cocktail prison officer finally enjoyed on Thames, perhaps?

parts.note: screw is British slang for a prison warder

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of enjoyed

parts.note: the Thames is an example of a river

explanation.surface: A prison guard sipping a cocktail he enjoyed while out on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwdriver is a mixed drink of vodka and orange juice.

clue.text: Authority, for example?

definitions.meaning: having a ... is having power or influence in a decision
... is used to introduce an example, as in 'take, ..., Paris'

explanation.definitionFit: The word serves both as a noun for influence and as a word introducing instances.

clue.text: Lover to get shot of in Derby

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or broken, so these letters are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone wants to get rid of their lover while at the Derby races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get shot of' looks like an idiom for getting rid of, but only 'shot' signals the anagram of OF IN DERBY.
explanation.definitionFit: A boyfriend is a male romantic partner, a person one loves.

clue.text: Agreeable type met at first in the old sickbay

parts.note: ye is an old spelling of the

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the word for sickbay

parts.note: san, short for sanatorium, is a school sickbay

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of met

explanation.surface: A cheerful type first met in an old-fashioned infirmary.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes man always agrees with superiors, an obsequiously agreeable sort.

clue.text: Arbitrary amount given to Scottish queen

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money
Mary, Queen of Scots

explanation.surface: An arbitrary sum of money handed to Mary, Queen of Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Summary justice is dealt out without formal process, so summary can mean arbitrary.

clue.text: Exchange involving humorist in school

indicators.note: involving means the abbreviation for school wraps round the humorist

parts.note: a wit is a person of clever humour

explanation.surface: A trade involving a comedian at a school.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch is to swap or trade one thing for another.

clue.text: Downcast, had gong replaced

indicators.note: replaced signals the letters of the two words are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone dejected because the gong they had was replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog look is shamefaced and dejected, much like being downcast.

clue.text: Categorically declare a sure winner on radio?

indicators.note: on radio means the phrase is heard spoken, as broadcast

parts.note: the indefinite article, A; a cert is racing slang for a certainty, a horse sure to win

explanation.surface: A racing commentator on the radio insists a horse is bound to win.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert is to state something firmly and confidently as fact.

clue.text: Philanderer more sensible to skirt Arab country

indicators.note: to skirt is to go round the edges, so the comparative surrounds the country

parts.note: wiser means more sensible
Oman is a country of the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A womaniser wiser than to chase skirt in an Arab country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirt' plays on its slang sense of women, apt for a philanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A womaniser is a man who has many casual affairs, the same as a philanderer.

clue.text: Wife takes a long time to get pay

parts.note: ages means a long time

explanation.surface: A wife waits for ages to receive her pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Wages are the pay received for work, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Close relative's unfinished vocal piece

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word for a vocal piece is dropped

parts.note: a song is a piece of music for voice

explanation.surface: A relative's song left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after relative stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A son is a male child, one of the closest family relations.

clue.text: Ragout served by girl on motorway

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A stew served up by a girl at a motorway café.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 runs from London to Leeds; the digit 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A salmi is a rich ragout of game birds, a kind of stew.

clue.text: VIP's girl seen following older relative

indicators.note: following puts the girl after the relative

parts.note: gran is a grandmother
Dee is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An important person's girlfriend spotted walking behind her grandmother.
explanation.walkthrough: VIP's means 'VIP is'; seen is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a person of high rank and influence, a very important person.

clue.text: Some primeval idea having legal authority

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An ancient idea that still carries the force of law.
explanation.definitionFit: A valid document or contract is legally binding and enforceable.

clue.text: Asian bean plant, one originally unknown in South Africa

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the abbreviation for South Africa
originally takes the first letter of one

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: An Asian bean plant, of which one was at first unknown in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Soya is the legume native to East Asia, grown for its edible beans.

clue.text: Speckled bird gazing fixedly across lake

indicators.note: across means the word for gazing stretches over the lake letter, holding it inside

parts.note: staring is gazing fixedly

explanation.surface: A spotted bird stares intently across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The starling is a common songbird with glossy plumage flecked with pale spots.
